items.title: State restores $200 million, fully funding long-planned Miami-to-Aventura commuter train
items.desc: The 'Northeast Corridor' train line has been promised to residents of North Dade for decades, but it has struggled to assemble the funding needed to make it happen.

headlines: STATE RESTORES $200 MILLION TO FULLY FUND MIAMI-AVENTURA TRAIN
NORTHEAST CORRIDOR COMMUTER TRAIN SECURES FULL CONSTRUCTION FUNDING
FIVE MIAMI NEIGHBORHOODS TO GET NEW COMMUTER RAIL ACCESS
draft.article:
A long-awaited commuter rail connection between downtown Miami and Aventura has reached full funding after the Florida Department of Transportation restored $200 million to its five-year transit work plan. The restored state allocation fills the final gap for the $927.3 million Northeast Corridor project.

Miami-Dade County has pledged $337.9 million toward the line, backed by $389 million in federal funding. Running from MiamiCentral along Florida East Coast Railway tracks, the public transit line plans to build five new stations serving Wynwood, the Miami Design District, Little Haiti, North Miami, and near Florida International University's Biscayne Bay campus.

The route will serve as the first leg of the planned 85-mile regional Coastal Link.

items.desc: A girl was rushed to Jackson Memorial after her family's pit bull bit her — then the dog fled before deputies could stop it.

headlines: GIRL HOSPITALIZED AFTER PIT BULL ATTACK IN NORTHWEST MIAMI-DADE
FAMILY PIT BULL BITES CHILD THEN ESCAPES IN MIAMI-DADE
SEARCH UNDERWAY ACROSS NORTHWEST MIAMI-DADE AFTER CHILD ATTACKED AT HOME
draft.article:
A young girl was rushed to Jackson Memorial Hospital on Wednesday night after being bitten by her family's American pit bull inside a home in northwest Miami-Dade. Emergency crews and Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office deputies rushed to the 1700 block of Northwest 66th Street, where a neighbor reported seeing the child bleeding heavily from her arm.

When deputies arrived at the property, the animal moved toward them. Deputies deployed a Taser to prevent another attack, but the dog was not struck and fled the scene.

Security cameras later captured a dog matching its description roaming nearby streets. The girl's condition remains unknown, and the dog has not yet been located.

items.title: Need a ride? How Freebee grew to fill gaps across South Florida

headlines: FREEBEE EXPANDS TO OVER TWO MILLION FREE RIDES ANNUALLY
MIAMI BEACH ELECTRIC SHUTTLE GROWS ACROSS FLORIDA
HOW TWO UM GRADS BUILT A FREE MIAMI TRANSIT NETWORK
draft.article:
What began nearly fifteen years ago in Miami Beach with just six electric carts has grown into a massive regional transit service. University of Miami graduates Jason Spiegel and Kris Kimball originally created Freebee as an ad-supported ride service, giving free trips around South Beach and Brickell before launching an on-demand app in 2015.

A partnership with Key Biscayne in 2017 pivoted the company toward government contracts. Today, Freebee runs over 300 vehicles across more than 50 communities, providing over two million free neighborhood rides each year. Following a merger last month with autonomous vehicle company Beep, the combined operation will employ nearly 1,000 workers across more than 60 communities.

headlines: EARLY VOTING BEGINS OCTOBER 19 IN MIAMI-DADE AND BROWARD
SOUTH FLORIDA EARLY VOTING OPENS FOR MIDTERM ELECTIONS
MIAMI VOTERS GET FOURTEEN DAYS TO CAST EARLY BALLOTS
draft.article:
Early voting opens Monday, Oct. 19, for registered voters across Miami-Dade and Broward counties ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Local residents have 14 consecutive days to cast their ballots, with polling stations remaining open through Nov. 1. Voters are not restricted to their precinct and can cast a ballot at any designated early voting site in their county of registration. Participating locations include area public libraries, government buildings, and community centers, operating between eight and 12 hours daily.

Voters must present an accepted form of current photo identification featuring a signature, such as a Florida driver's license or U.S. passport.

HOW OUR COUNTY AND FORT DALLAS BEGAN IN 1836

Dade County officially came into existence on February 4, 1836. The county was founded and named in honor of Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River.

That exact same year brought major foundational history to our local waterways. Fort Dallas was constructed in 1836 to function as a military base during the Second Seminole War.

From the building of military posts like Fort Dallas to early community designations along the Miami River, 1836 remains a crucial year that marked the official beginnings of the county.
